head: Banking app security issues: half of 2,686 apps had serious flaws
dek: Security firm Ostorlab tested 2,686 mobile banking apps from 487 banks in 64 countries and found that 51.5% had at least one high or critical security problem. Its scanner got past the fingerprint or face login in 35.1% of the Android apps.
details: About one in five apps (20.3%) contained private keys, cloud passwords or access tokens inside the app. Only 4.9% supported passkeys, and 99.5% of the Android apps still run on Android versions that no longer get security updates. Ostorlab says a finding shows a problem is there, not that it can be used in a real attack, and the report names no banks.
where: Android, iPhone and HarmonyOS banking apps worldwide
means: If you bank on your phone, your bank's app may be less protected than you assume, and an old phone that no longer gets updates adds to the risk.
todo: Keep your phone's system and your bank app updated. If your bank offers passkeys, turn them on.
thumb_words: HALF OF BANKING APPS HAVE FLAWS
